toc.title: Storage accounts and the storage services
Moving files to and within Azure

html:
1Storage accounts and the storage services

An Azure storage account is a container that holds your storage services under one globally unique name (3 to 24 lowercase letters and numbers). Data is encrypted at rest by default and is reached over HTTPS.

Service What it stores Use it for
Azure Blob Storage Unstructured data (objects): documents, images, video, backups, logs Large amounts of files; serving content; backups; data lakes
Azure Files Fully managed file shares (SMB and NFS) Replace or extend on-premises file servers; shared drives; lift and shift
Azure Queue Storage Messages in a queue Pass messages between app components, asynchronous work
Azure Table Storage NoSQL key-attribute data (structured, no schema) Flexible datasets such as user data or device information
Azure Disk Storage (managed disks) Disks for virtual machines OS and data disks for VMs

Exam tip

. Match the data type: files → Blob (objects) or Files (shares); messages → Queue; structured NoSQL → Table; VM disks → Disk. A "file share mapped like a network drive" → Azure Files.

2Storage access tiers (Blob Storage)

Tiers trade storage cost against access cost and speed. You choose a tier by how often you read the data.

Tier Access Storage cost Access cost Minimum stay Notes
Hot Frequent Highest Lowest None Online, active data
Cool Infrequent Lower Higher 30 days Online, short-term backups
Cold Rare Lower still Higher still 90 days Online
Archive Almost never Lowest Highest 180 days Offline: data must be rehydrated (takes hours) before it can be read

[Verify live] for minimum periods and prices. The Archive tier can only be set per blob, and data in Archive cannot be read directly.

Exam tip

. "Data accessed rarely, lowest storage cost, can wait hours to read" → Archive. "Frequently accessed" → Hot. The cheaper the storage, the more it costs to read.

3Redundancy options

Azure keeps multiple copies of your data to protect against failures. You choose how far apart they are.

Option Copies Where Protects from
LRS (locally redundant) 3 One datacenter in one region Server rack or drive failure
ZRS (zone-redundant) 3 Three or more availability zones in one region A datacenter (zone) failure
GRS (geo-redundant) 6 LRS in the primary region, plus LRS in a paired secondary region A regional disaster
GZRS (geo-zone-redundant) 6 ZRS in the primary region, plus LRS in a secondary region Zone failure and regional disaster
RA-GRS / RA-GZRS 6 Same as GRS / GZRS, plus read access to the secondary Regional disaster, with reads from the secondary

  • Local and zone options keep data in one region; geo options also copy it to a paired region.
  • The secondary of GRS/GZRS is not readable unless you choose the read-access (RA) variant, or a failover happens.
Exam tip

. Cheapest = LRS. Datacenter failure = ZRS. Regional disaster = GRS or GZRS. Read from the secondary = RA-. Copies in a different region always mean a geo option.

4Storage account options

Option Choices
Performance Standard (hard disk, general purpose) or Premium (solid state, low latency)
Account types General-purpose v2 (the standard type for most scenarios: blobs, files, queues, tables); Premium accounts for block blobs, file shares or page blobs, for high-performance needs
Redundancy LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS, and the read-access variants
Access tier (default) Hot or Cool

Use Premium when the workload needs consistently low latency and high transaction rates.

5Moving files to and within Azure

Tool What it does Notes
AzCopy A command-line tool to copy blobs and files to or from a storage account Good for scripts and large copies
Azure Storage Explorer A graphical application to browse and manage storage accounts (blobs, files, queues, tables) Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
Azure File Sync Syncs on-premises Windows file servers with Azure Files and caches frequently used files locally Keeps the on-premises server as a fast cache while data lives in Azure

6Migration options

Option What it does
Azure Migrate A central hub of tools to discover, assess and migrate on-premises servers, databases, web apps and virtual desktops to Azure
Azure Data Box A physical, ruggedized device Microsoft ships to you: you load data offline and send it back to be uploaded to Azure. Used for large amounts of data or slow networks (Data Box Disk, Data Box, Data Box Heavy)
Exam tip

. Servers and apps → Azure Migrate. Terabytes of data with limited bandwidth → Azure Data Box. Keep a local file server cache → Azure File Sync. Copy with a command → AzCopy. Click-and-browse tool → Storage Explorer.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors needs a shared network drive in Azure that on-premises servers can map using SMB. Which service fits?

  • AAzure Blob Storage
  • BAzure Queue Storage
  • CAzure Files
  • DAzure Table Storage
Show the answer

Answer: C. Azure Files provides managed file shares using SMB (and NFS). Blob stores unstructured objects.

S2Data must be kept for years, is almost never read, and the lowest storage cost matters more than read speed. Which tier fits?

  • AArchive
  • BHot
  • CCool
  • DPremium
Show the answer

Answer: A. Archive has the lowest storage cost; data is offline and must be rehydrated, which takes hours.

S3A company needs its data copied to another region so it survives a regional disaster. Which redundancy option provides this?

  • ALRS
  • BGRS
  • CZRS
  • DHot
Show the answer

Answer: B. GRS (or GZRS) copies data to a secondary region. LRS and ZRS stay in one region.

S4A company must move 200 TB to Azure over a slow network. What is the best option?

  • AAzCopy over the internet
  • BAzure Storage Explorer
  • CAzure Data Box
  • DAzure DNS
Show the answer

Answer: C. Data Box transports large data volumes offline on a physical device.

S5Which tool synchronizes an on-premises Windows file server with Azure Files?

  • AAzure Migrate
  • BAzCopy
  • CAzure Advisor
  • DAzure File Sync
Show the answer

Answer: D. Azure File Sync keeps file servers and Azure Files in sync with local caching.

S6Which storage service holds messages that application components pass to each other?

  • AAzure Table Storage
  • BAzure Files
  • CAzure Queue Storage
  • DAzure Disk Storage
Show the answer

Answer: C. Queue Storage stores messages for asynchronous communication.

S7Which redundancy option protects against the loss of a single datacenter by spreading copies across availability zones?

  • ALRS
  • BArchive
  • CCool
  • DZRS
Show the answer

Answer: D. ZRS keeps three copies in three zones of one region.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Which storage service is for unstructured objects?

Show the answer

Azure Blob Storage.

R2Name the four blob tiers.

Show the answer

Hot, Cool, Cold and Archive.

R3Which tier is offline and needs rehydration?

Show the answer

Archive.

R4How many copies do LRS and ZRS keep?

Show the answer

Three copies each (LRS in one datacenter, ZRS across three zones).

R5What does the RA prefix add to GRS?

Show the answer

Read access to the secondary region.

R6AzCopy or Storage Explorer: which is command line?

Show the answer

AzCopy.

R7Which service discovers and assesses on-premises servers for migration?

Show the answer

Azure Migrate.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Services Blob = objects; Files = SMB/NFS shares; Queue = messages; Table = NoSQL; Disk = VM disks
Tiers Hot (frequent) → Cool (30 days) → Cold (90 days) → Archive (180 days, offline, rehydrate)
Redundancy LRS 3 copies one datacenter; ZRS three zones; GRS/GZRS add a paired region; RA = read access to the secondary
Account standard general-purpose v2 for most; premium for low latency; globally unique name
Move files AzCopy (command line); Storage Explorer (GUI); File Sync (on-premises file server cache)
Migrate Azure Migrate (servers, databases, apps); Data Box (offline, huge data)
